items.title: entry: Relate nucleotide composition to nucleic-acid structure
items.prompt: A molecule contains ribose bonded to adenine but has no phosphate group. Which classification is most specific?
options: A nucleoside composed of a sugar and a purine base
A nucleotide composed only of phosphate and a purine base
A phosphodiester-linked polymer containing several residues
A pyrimidine residue attached directly to a phosphate backbone
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: guided: Relate nucleotide composition to nucleic-acid structure
items.prompt: In a nucleic-acid strand, which repeating connection forms the main covalent path along the polymer?
options: Purine-pyrimidine-purine connections joined through base rings
Sugar-phosphate-sugar connections joined by phosphodiester bonds
Base-phosphate-base connections that omit every pentose sugar
Sugar-base-sugar connections joined by hydrogen bonds
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: light: Relate nucleotide composition to nucleic-acid structure
items.prompt: A labelled residue has deoxyribose, phosphate, and a fused two-ring nitrogenous base. Which description fits the residue?
options: An RNA nucleoside carrying a pyrimidine but no phosphate
A backbone made entirely from fused purine ring systems
A DNA nucleotide carrying a purine base that projects from the backbone
A DNA sugar that replaces both the phosphate and the base
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: solo: Relate nucleotide composition to nucleic-acid structure
items.prompt: A DNA coding-strand segment is 5′-ATG-3′. An RNA strand preserving that information is written 5′→3′. Which option gives both the RNA sequence and its residue chemistry?
options: 5′-ATG-3′ with ribose and thymine
3′-UAC-5′ with ribose and uracil
5′-TAC-3′ with deoxyribose and thymine
5′-AUG-3′ with ribose and uracil
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: near: Relate nucleotide composition to nucleic-acid structure
items.prompt: A polymer diagram shows a two-ring base attached to a sugar that is linked to phosphates on both sides. Which interpretation is correct?
options: The base is a purine residue projecting from a sugar-phosphate backbone
The base is a pyrimidine that forms the complete covalent backbone
The sugar is a base residue held to phosphate only by hydrogen bonds
The phosphates are side groups while linked bases form the main chain
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: changed: Relate nucleotide composition to nucleic-acid structure

The sugar-phosphate backbone is interrupted at that position
All deoxyribose units are immediately changed into ribose units
The strand gains an extra base without changing its covalent path
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: repair near: Relate nucleotide composition to nucleic-acid structure

It replaces the pentose sugar whenever the residue is a purine
It attaches to a backbone sugar and projects away from the repeating chain
It connects adjacent phosphates while every sugar remains a side group
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

As a pyrimidine residue attached to ribose and projecting from the backbone

items.title: entry: Explain semiconservative DNA replication
items.prompt: After a DNA duplex opens, what is the direct role of each separated parental strand?
options: It serves as a template for synthesis of a complementary new strand
It is discarded so both daughter molecules contain only new DNA
It joins the other parental strand without any nucleotide synthesis
It acts as a primer that polymerase extends without a free end
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: guided: Explain semiconservative DNA replication
items.prompt: Which sequence correctly orders the core actions at a newly activated replication origin?
options: Ligase opens DNA, polymerase removes primers, helicase seals fragments
Helicase opens DNA, primase supplies a primer, polymerase extends, ligase seals
Polymerase starts without a primer, then primase unwinds the duplex
Primase seals fragments, helicase adds bases, ligase copies templates
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: light: Explain semiconservative DNA replication
items.prompt: A fork opens normally and primers form, but no complementary DNA is added. Which core activity is most directly defective?
options: Helicase separation of the parental strands at the fork
Primase production of the short starting nucleic-acid segment
DNA polymerase extension from the primer's free 3′ end
Ligase sealing of adjacent fragments after synthesis finishes
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: solo: Explain semiconservative DNA replication
items.prompt: A parental duplex has one strand labelled blue and one labelled gold. After semiconservative replication, how are the labels distributed?
options: One daughter receives both labelled strands and the other receives two new strands
Both labels are cut into pieces and mixed through every new strand
All four daughter strands retain the parental labels after copying
Each daughter duplex has one labelled parental strand and one unlabelled new strand
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: near: Explain semiconservative DNA replication
items.prompt: Which daughter-strand pattern is the defining result of semiconservative DNA replication?
options: Each daughter duplex contains one parental strand and one newly synthesized strand
One daughter contains both parental strands while the other contains both new strands
Every daughter strand contains alternating pieces of parental and new DNA
Both daughter duplexes contain only parental strands with no synthesis
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: changed: Explain semiconservative DNA replication
items.prompt: Most origins on a long eukaryotic chromosome are disabled, but the remaining origins and forks work normally. What is the most direct consequence?
options: Every daughter duplex becomes conservative rather than semiconservative
Fewer regions begin copying concurrently, so completion takes longer
Polymerase reverses direction and begins synthesizing DNA three-prime to five-prime
Ligase becomes the enzyme that opens all remaining origins
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: repair near: Explain semiconservative DNA replication

Follow each intact parental strand into a daughter and identify its new complement
Assume both parental strands remain together because they began paired

items.title: entry: Explain chromosome-end replication
items.prompt: Why can DNA polymerase not begin a new strand at an arbitrary unprimed position?
options: It requires an existing free 3′ end to extend
It can add nucleotides only to a free 5′ end
It must first join two chromosome ends with ligase
It can copy DNA only after every base is removed
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: guided: Explain chromosome-end replication
items.prompt: After the final primer at a linear chromosome end is removed, which feature creates the end-replication problem?
options: The parental template is converted entirely into RNA
No upstream DNA 3′ end remains from which to fill the terminal gap
Every internal phosphodiester bond is broken at once
Complementary base-pair specificity stops operating at chromosome ends

items.title: light: Explain chromosome-end replication
items.prompt: Which primer-removal gap can conventional polymerase most directly fill?
options: A terminal gap beyond the last available DNA 3′ end
A gap after both template and new strand have been removed
An internal gap with an adjacent upstream DNA 3′ end
A terminal gap containing no template information at all
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: solo: Explain chromosome-end replication
items.prompt: What is the expected cumulative effect of many replication cycles without specialized chromosome-end maintenance?

All chromosome ends fuse into one continuous circular molecule

The terminal DNA becomes progressively shorter

items.title: near: Explain chromosome-end replication

items.title: entry: Explain DNA repair

items.title: solo: Explain DNA repair
